content: Fleet management software allows dispatchers to track vehicles in real-time, optimizing routes and minimizing idle times, while SCADA systems provide critical telemetry data regarding the status of automated machinery, ventilation systems, and power distribution networks. Together with two-way radio integration, these technologies ensure that dispatchers maintain continuous situational awareness. The main operational benefit derived from these dispatch and control room systems is enhanced operational efficiency and centralized monitoring, enabling mining companies to streamline their daily activities and reduce operational bottlenecks. The efficacy of these dispatch operations is heavily dependent on the quality and reliability of the underlying communication networks. Traditional communication methods have increasingly demonstrated inadequacies in meeting the connectivity requirements of underground and large-scale mining activities [42] . Consequently, the industry has prioritized the adoption of modern cellular and network-based solutions to address historical operational inefficiencies and safety concerns [42] . Advanced systems are essential for fostering better coordination and a secure mining ecosystem . In alignment with this technological shift, smart communication solutions have been introduced, offering technologies such as Push-to-Talk over Cellular (PoC) to ensure high-speed, mission-critical connectivity across mine sites [44] . Such features are indispensable for dispatch and control room operations, which require reliable and unified communication platforms to manage personnel and equipment effectively [44] . Furthermore, the physical hardware deployed in these settings must withstand extreme industrial conditions. Robust equipment capable of noise immunity and seamless integration is vital for both daily operations and emergencies, affirming the industry’s reliance on dependable communication infrastructures [41] . Key technologies and protocols underpinning these emergency systems include underground distress beacons, Terrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA) networks, and evacuation Public Address (PA) systems. Underground distress beacons serve as a vital lifeline, allowing trapped or endangered miners to signal their location to surface rescue teams. TETRA networks provide secure, resilient, and independent communication channels that remain operational even if standard cellular or Wi-Fi networks fail during an incident.
